name: Advanced Encryption Patterns
description: This module describes advanced patterns for encryption intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.
content:
This module describes advanced patterns for encryption intended for non-trivial cases where the basic approach is insufficient.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any encryption bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Prefer the simplest encryption approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. Document any non-obvious encryption decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
4. Prefer explicit, readable encryption solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Validate encryption outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. When multiple encryption strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen encryption approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. When encryption guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Keep encryption changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated encryption concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new encryption abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop encryption edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about encryption over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
